claims.subject: relationship--kimsuky--overlaps-with--e6ee0ddce0fdccac
claims.statement: Kimsuky overlaps-with APT43: MITRE treats APT43 as an associated Kimsuky group name, while Mandiant defines APT43 using its own collection scope. The overlap is well supported, but exact one-to-one identity is not.
claims.verification_rationale: Verified OSINT relationship: status=partially-supported; limitation=Vendor collection boundaries differ; do not replace both profiles with a single exact alias record. counterevidence=The sources support overlap but do not establish that every APT43 observation belongs to the narrower Kimsuky activity set.
counterevidence: Verified OSINT relationship: status=partially-supported; limitation=Vendor collection boundaries differ; do not replace both profiles with a single exact alias record. counterevidence=The sources support overlap but do not establish that every APT43 observation belongs to the narrower Kimsuky activity set.

claims.subject: relationship--kimsuky--mitre--0d19277262804fd6
claims.statement: Kimsuky overlaps-with Lazarus Group: DPRK threat actor cluster boundaries overlap in open source reporting, with some security researchers consolidating all attributed North Korean state-sponsored cyber activity under [Lazarus Group](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0032), rather than tracking operationally distinct subgroups.
claims.verification_rationale: MITRE relationship extraction: status=supported; A narrative cross-reference establishes a relationship but does not by itself prove exact actor identity or identical scope.
